entries.title: How does moving your body help it work well?
entries.answer: When you move enough to breathe faster, your heart and lungs are moving more oxygen around your body. Over time, regular movement can help them do those jobs well. Moving your body also makes muscles work. Some activities, such as running and hopping, give your bones a reason to keep building strong material. Movement comes in many forms. Playing an active game, walking, and dancing are everyday ways to use your muscles and practice moving with control.
facts: Walking, dancing, and many kinds of play can all count as physical activity.

entries.title: How does vitamin D help bones?
entries.answer: Vitamin D helps your gut take in calcium from food. Calcium is one of the materials your body uses to build strong bones and teeth. Some foods, such as several kinds of fish, naturally contain vitamin D. It may be added to other foods, and your skin can also make some when sunlight reaches it. Vitamin D and calcium do different jobs. One helps calcium get into the body, and the other becomes part of the hard material in bones.
facts: Some foods contain added vitamin D.

entries.title: What are carbohydrates?
entries.answer: A potato, a pear, and a piece of bread can all provide carbohydrates. Some carbohydrates are sugars, such as the ones that help make a ripe pear sweet. Others are starches, long chains your body can break into smaller sugars. Cells can use those sugars for energy. Plant foods can also contain fiber, a kind of carbohydrate that passes much farther through your gut without being broken up by your own digestive juices.
facts: Sugars, starches, and fiber are all kinds of carbohydrates.

entries.title: What can a food label tell you?
entries.answer: Foods sold in many packages have a Nutrition Facts label. It lists certain materials in a stated amount of food, such as its fiber, protein, or iron. The list helps you compare foods if you pay attention to how much food the numbers describe. Two packages might use different serving sizes. A separate list of ingredients tells you what went into the food. The label can answer some useful questions even though it cannot tell you whether you will like the food.
facts: A Nutrition Facts label usually reports how much fiber one serving contains.

entries.title: What does handwashing wash away?
entries.answer: A hand can look clean and still have material from things it touched. Some of that material clings to natural oils on the skin. Water alone may run over it without carrying it all away. Soap helps loosen oily material, and rubbing reaches folds and spots such as the skin between your fingers. Rinsing carries away the loosened material. That is why soap, rubbing, and rinsing each have a job in the same wash.
facts: Soap and rubbing help loosen material before water rinses it away.

entries.title: What does serving size mean on a package?
entries.answer: The serving size on a Nutrition Facts label tells you how much food the numbers refer to. It might be a cup, several crackers, or another amount. It is based on how much people often eat at a time, so it is not an order to eat exactly that much. If a pouch contains two servings and you look at the whole pouch, you may have to double numbers that are shown for one serving.
facts: One package can hold more than one serving.

entries.title: What does sleep do for you?
entries.answer: When you sleep, you are less aware of the things around you, but your body and brain keep working. Your brain goes through several kinds of sleep in a repeating pattern. Sleep helps with memory and attention, so it can be harder to concentrate after a night of poor rest. Your body does many ordinary upkeep jobs while you sleep too. How much sleep a person needs changes as they grow, and the hours you are in bed do not always match the hours you are asleep.
facts: Several kinds of sleep repeat during a typical night.

entries.title: What does vitamin C do?
entries.answer: Vitamin C helps your body make an important protein for skin and other tissues. It can also help your body take in iron from some plant foods. That is one reason foods with vitamin C can be useful as part of a varied meal. An orange is a familiar example, but it is far from the only source. Other fruits and some vegetables contain vitamin C as well. People need to get it from what they eat or drink.
facts: Bell peppers and oranges are examples of foods that can provide vitamin C.

entries.title: What does your body do with fat from food?
entries.answer: Fat is a kind of nutrient found in foods such as nuts, fish, and cooking oils. It can provide energy. Some of the bits made during digestion become building materials for the outside of your cells. Fat can also help the body take in certain vitamins. Different foods contain different kinds of fat. Inside the small intestine, bile and digestive juices work together so the body can take in parts of the fat you ate.
facts: Some vitamins are easier for your body to take in when fat is present.

entries.title: What is fiber in food?
entries.answer: Fiber is material from plants that your body has trouble breaking down with its own digestive juices. You might eat some when you have an apple, oatmeal, or beans. Some kinds of fiber soak up water and become thick. Others can add bulk to what moves through your gut. Tiny living things in your large intestine can also use some kinds. Two foods with the same amount of fiber do not always contain exactly the same kinds of fiber.
facts: Whole grains, beans, fruits, and vegetables can provide fiber.

entries.title: What makes a grain whole?
entries.answer: A grain kernel has an outer coat, a part that can start a new plant, and a large store of food for that plant. A whole grain keeps all three parts. They can still be present if the grain is rolled flat or ground into flour. To make some kinds of refined flour, the mill takes away much of the outer coat and the part that would grow. This changes which kinds of nutrients and how much fiber stay in the flour.
facts: Whole oats and brown rice are examples of whole grains.

entries.title: What protects the outside of a tooth?
entries.answer: The part of a tooth that sticks above your gums wears a hard coat called enamel. It is tough enough to protect the tooth through lots of biting and chewing. Some bacteria in the mouth can make acids when they use sugars and starches. Over time, repeated contact with those acids can take minerals out of enamel. If enough damage adds up, a hole called a cavity can form. Fluoride can help teeth resist this kind of damage.
facts: The hard outer coat on the part of a tooth you can see is called enamel.

entries.title: Why are beans useful in meals?
entries.answer: Many of the beans people eat are seeds that grow in pods. Peas and lentils come from related plants. People use them in soups, stews, salads, and spreads. They supply protein along with fiber. That combination makes them different from foods that give you protein without fiber, such as an egg. Dried beans can be kept for later in a suitable dry place and are often cooked before eating. Some kinds also come already cooked in a can.
facts: Chickpeas, dry peas, and lentils are all foods in the legume family.

entries.title: Why does your body need iron?
entries.answer: Iron is a metal that can be part of materials in your body, even though it does not look like a nail or a piece of steel there. Red blood cells use it in hemoglobin, which picks up oxygen as blood flows past the lungs. Iron in food helps supply what the body needs for jobs like this. Foods such as beans, meat, and some cereals with added iron can provide it in different forms.
facts: Iron is part of the oxygen-carrying protein hemoglobin.

entries.title: Why does your body need protein?
entries.answer: Protein does many jobs in the body. Some proteins help form muscles. Others act like tiny tools that speed up changes inside you. When you eat foods such as eggs, fish, or beans, your gut breaks much of their protein into smaller parts. Those parts are called amino acids. Cells can join them in different orders to make the proteins they need. Think of the pieces of a train set being used to build a different sort of train.
facts: Beans, eggs, fish, nuts, and other foods can provide protein.

entries.title: Why does your body need vitamins?
entries.answer: Vitamins are substances you need in small amounts. Different vitamins help with different jobs. Some are involved when the body builds tissue or changes food into forms it can use. Although vitamins help the body use food, they are not a source of energy like sugar or fat. Foods contain different mixtures of vitamins. Some vitamins dissolve in water, while others dissolve in fat. That difference affects how the body takes them in and keeps them.
facts: The body can take in some vitamins with the help of fat.

entries.title: Why does your body need water?
entries.answer: Water is part of your blood and of the cells all through your body. It helps carry materials and helps you stay at a workable temperature. You lose water in sweat, in urine, and from the air you breathe out. What you drink and some of what you eat can replace it. You might notice that you feel thirsty after running around on a warm day. Your body uses more than one clue to keep the amount of water it holds in balance.
facts: Water leaves your body in ways you can see, such as sweat, and in the air you breathe out.

entries.title: Why is calcium important for bones?
entries.answer: Calcium is a mineral nutrient. Inside your body, much of it goes into the hard material in bones and teeth. It has other jobs too. A small amount travels through the blood and helps nerves send messages and muscles move. Calcium can come from foods such as yogurt, certain greens, or drinks with calcium added. The amount in a serving can depend on the particular food. Your body uses calcium over time as it maintains living tissue.
facts: Most of the calcium in your body is found in your bones and teeth.
